mechanism: Agents expose observable {{signal}}s through their actions and adjust subsequent actions in response to what they observe, without negotiating an explicit agreement. Compatible responses reinforce the observed signal; active counter-signals may {{dampen}} it, and unreinforced alignment strength undergoes {{decay}}. Alignment is inferred from the resulting pattern of repeated mutual adjustment.
failure_modes: False Resonance: Apparent alignment that is actually random {{noise}}.
Echo Chamber: Feedback {{loop}} amplifies error instead of {{signal}}.
Adversarial imitation: agents emit actions or {{signal}}s crafted to mimic compatibility without corresponding alignment.
Precise-coordination mismatch: RESONATE only achieves approximate alignment; high-stakes actions requiring precision need a different coordination primitive.
invariants: Each reinforcing or dampening adjustment responds to a previously observed {{signal}}.
Repeated compatible responses increase alignment strength; for the same responses, a larger `amplification_factor` cannot produce a smaller increase.
Absent reinforcement, alignment strength does not increase; its attenuation follows `signal_decay`.
postconditions: Local alignment cluster formed OR dispersed

parameters.name: amplification_factor
parameters.description: How much repeated alignment signals boost coordination strength

parameters.name: signal_decay
parameters.description: Rate at which unconfirmed alignment signals weaken over time
